events.title: First peoples in the Andes
events.description: Hunter-gatherers occupy caves at Pikimachay and the high puna, among the earliest human presence in South America.

events.title: Guitarrero Cave occupied
events.description: Highland foragers in the Callejon de Huaylas leave some of the oldest textiles and cultivated beans in the Americas.

events.title: Domestication of Andean crops begins
events.description: Potato, quinoa, squash and chilli are brought into cultivation, the foundation of every later Andean society.

events.title: Camelid herding in the highlands
events.description: Llama and alpaca are domesticated, giving the Andes transport, wool and meat without draught animals or the wheel.

events.title: Chinchorro mummification on the coast
events.description: Coastal peoples practise deliberate mummification thousands of years before Egypt.

events.title: Cotton and fishing nets on the coast
events.description: Cotton cultivation supports net fishing, and the rich Humboldt current feeds the first large coastal settlements.

events.title: Caral built in the Supe valley
events.description: The oldest known city in the Americas rises with sunken plazas and six pyramids, contemporary with the Egyptian pyramids.

events.title: Norte Chico civilisation flourishes
events.description: Around thirty monumental sites along the Peruvian coast form the earliest complex society in the hemisphere, apparently without pottery or warfare.

events.title: Sechin Bajo and the coastal temples
events.description: Monumental architecture spreads; carvings at Cerro Sechin depict warriors and dismembered captives.

events.title: Pottery and maize arrive
events.description: Ceramics and maize agriculture spread through the Andes, changing diet and storage.

events.title: Kotosh religious tradition
events.description: Highland temples with crossed-hands reliefs mark early Andean ritual practice.

events.title: Chavin de Huantar founded
events.description: A temple complex at the meeting of two rivers becomes the pilgrimage centre of the first pan-Andean religious movement.

events.title: The Lanzon installed
events.description: A carved granite deity stands at the heart of Chavin's underground galleries, part feline, part serpent, part human.

events.title: Chavin art style spreads
events.description: Jaguar and caiman motifs appear on textiles, gold and pottery from the coast to the highlands, unifying the region culturally.

events.title: Goldworking at Chongoyape
events.description: Andean smiths master hammering, soldering and alloying, producing crowns and ornaments of remarkable sophistication.

events.title: Paracas culture on the south coast
events.description: Paracas weavers produce embroidered mantles of a technical quality never surpassed in the Andes.

events.title: Trepanation practised in the Andes
events.description: Paracas surgeons cut into skulls to treat injuries, and many patients demonstrably survived.

events.title: Pukara emerges near Titicaca
events.description: A highland centre on the altiplano develops the sunken court and stone sculpture traditions later taken up by Tiwanaku.

events.title: Chavin influence collapses
events.description: The pilgrimage network breaks down and regional cultures assert themselves across the Andes.

events.title: Nazca culture begins
events.description: On the arid south coast the Nazca develop polychrome pottery and an elaborate underground aqueduct system.

events.title: Puquios aqueducts dug
events.description: Spiral wells and underground channels tap groundwater and still irrigate fields in the Nazca valley today.

events.title: Nazca Lines created
events.description: Enormous geoglyphs of animals and straight lines are scraped into the desert over several centuries. Their purpose is still debated.

events.title: Moche state forms on the north coast
events.description: Warrior-priest rulers govern irrigated valleys from adobe pyramids, the most powerful society of its day in the Americas.

events.title: Huaca del Sol and Huaca de la Luna built
events.description: The two great adobe platforms outside modern Trujillo hold painted murals and evidence of ritual sacrifice.

events.title: Moche portrait pottery
events.description: Moche potters produce startlingly individual ceramic portraits, unique in pre-Columbian art.

events.title: Tiwanaku rises on the altiplano
events.description: A ceremonial city near Lake Titicaca develops raised-field agriculture at 3,800 metres and begins expanding its influence.

events.title: Lord of Sipan buried
events.description: A Moche ruler is interred with gold, turquoise and attendants. The tomb, found intact in 1987, is the richest in the Americas.

events.title: Prolonged drought and El Nino floods
events.description: Decades of climatic disruption undermine Moche irrigation and precipitate political crisis.

events.title: Moche capital shifts to Pampa Grande
events.description: Power moves inland as the coastal centres decline under environmental and military pressure.

events.title: Wari expands from Ayacucho
events.description: A highland state builds walled administrative centres and a road network across much of Peru.

events.title: Nazca culture declines
events.description: Deforestation of huarango woodland and drought bring the south coast society to an end.

events.title: Wari terracing transforms agriculture
events.description: Systematic terracing and canal irrigation open steep highland slopes to farming, supporting far denser populations.

events.title: Pikillacta built
events.description: A vast rectilinear Wari settlement near Cusco houses administrators in hundreds of identical compounds.

events.title: Tiwanaku at its height
events.description: The city dominates the Titicaca basin and the trade routes to the Pacific and the eastern lowlands.

events.title: Quipu record-keeping in use
events.description: Knotted cord devices record numbers and possibly narrative, the Andean answer to writing.

events.title: Wari collapses
events.description: The administrative centres are abandoned and the Andes fragment into competing regional states.

events.title: Tiwanaku abandoned
events.description: Prolonged drought ends the altiplano state; its ruins remain a place of pilgrimage and Inca origin myth.

events.title: Chimu kingdom founded at Chan Chan
events.description: The Chimor state rises on the north coast and builds the largest adobe city in the world.

events.title: Chimu irrigation network
events.description: Inter-valley canals move water tens of kilometres, supporting a population far beyond what local rainfall allows.

events.title: Chancay and Ychsma on the central coast
events.description: Regional states flourish around Lima, and the oracle at Pachacamac draws pilgrims from across the Andes.

events.title: Kingdom of Cusco founded
events.description: Manco Capac is said to found the Inca line in the Cusco valley, at this stage one small polity among many.

events.title: Chachapoya build Kuelap
events.description: A cloud-forest people raise a walled citadel on a limestone ridge with over four hundred round houses.

events.title: Chimu conquer the northern valleys
events.description: Chimor expands to control a thousand kilometres of coastline, the largest state in the Andes before the Inca.

events.title: Sican goldwork at Batan Grande
events.description: The Lambayeque region produces gold funerary masks and tumi knives of extraordinary craftsmanship.

events.title: Inca defeat the Chanka
events.description: Pachacuti drives off the Chanka assault on Cusco, seizes power, and begins the imperial expansion.

events.title: Pachacuti rebuilds Cusco
events.description: The capital is remodelled in monumental stonework, reportedly laid out in the shape of a puma.

events.title: Machu Picchu built
events.description: A royal estate is raised on a ridge above the Urubamba, abandoned within a century and never found by the Spanish.

events.title: Sacsayhuaman begun
events.description: Cyclopean walls above Cusco are fitted without mortar so precisely that a blade cannot be inserted between the blocks.

events.title: Topa Inca conquers Chimor
events.description: The Chimu kingdom falls and its goldsmiths are resettled in Cusco.

events.title: The Qhapaq Nan road network
events.description: Some 40,000 kilometres of road with relay runners and storehouses bind the empire from Ecuador to Chile.

events.title: Mitma resettlement policy
events.description: Whole populations are moved to break resistance and spread Quechua, welding the empire together.

events.title: Huayna Capac becomes Sapa Inca
events.description: Tawantinsuyu reaches its greatest extent, ruling perhaps twelve million people.

events.title: Smallpox reaches the Andes
events.description: European disease arrives ahead of any European, killing Huayna Capac and his heir and gutting the population.

events.title: Civil war between Atahualpa and Huascar
events.description: The succession is contested and the empire tears itself apart on the eve of the Spanish arrival.

events.title: Capture of Atahualpa at Cajamarca
events.description: Pizarro's 168 men seize the emperor amid his army, then take the largest ransom in history and kill him anyway.

events.title: Spanish enter Cusco
events.description: The imperial capital is occupied and looted, its temples stripped of gold.

events.title: Lima founded
events.description: Pizarro establishes the City of Kings on the coast, orienting the colony towards Spain rather than the highlands.

events.title: Manco Inca besieges Cusco
events.description: A massive Inca rising nearly retakes the capital before withdrawing to Vilcabamba.

events.title: Pizarro assassinated
events.description: The conquistadors turn on each other; Pizarro is killed in Lima by rivals from the Almagro faction.

events.title: Silver found at Potosi
events.description: The mountain of silver funds the Spanish empire and consumes Andean lives on an industrial scale.

events.title: University of San Marcos founded
events.description: The oldest university in the Americas is chartered in Lima.

events.title: Viceroy Toledo arrives
events.description: Toledo reorganises the colony, forcing indigenous people into reducciones and systematising the mita labour draft.

events.title: Tupac Amaru executed
events.description: The last Inca ruler is beheaded in Cusco, ending the neo-Inca state at Vilcabamba.

events.title: Huaynaputina erupts
events.description: The largest volcanic eruption in South American history buries villages and darkens skies as far as Europe.

events.title: Garcilaso publishes the Royal Commentaries
events.description: The mestizo son of an Inca princess writes the first great account of the Andes from the inside.

events.title: Cusco School of painting
events.description: Indigenous and mestizo artists blend Andean motifs with European religious painting, gold leaf and all.

events.title: Earthquake devastates Lima
events.description: The capital is wrecked and the coastal agricultural economy shifts decisively northwards.

events.title: Viceroyalty of New Granada split off
events.description: Peru's territory and revenue shrink as Bourbon reformers redraw South America.

events.title: Lima and Callao destroyed
events.description: A great earthquake and tsunami kill thousands and level the port.

events.title: Tupac Amaru II rebellion
events.description: A cacique claiming Inca descent leads the largest indigenous rising in colonial America. It is crushed within two years.

events.title: Tupac Amaru II executed at Cusco
events.description: He is drawn and quartered in the main square; reprisals kill perhaps 100,000 people.

events.title: Napoleon invades Spain
events.description: The collapse of Spanish royal authority triggers independence movements across the Americas.

events.title: Cusco rebellion of Pumacahua
events.description: A creole and indigenous rising in the southern highlands is defeated, and Peru remains a royalist stronghold.

events.title: San Martin lands at Paracas
events.description: The Argentine liberator arrives by sea with a Chilean fleet to force the issue in royalist Peru.

events.title: Independence proclaimed in Lima
events.description: San Martin declares Peru independent, though royalist armies still hold the highlands.

events.title: Battle of Junin
events.description: Bolivar's cavalry defeat the royalists on the high plateau in an engagement fought without a shot.

events.title: Battle of Ayacucho
events.description: Sucre destroys the last royalist army, ending Spanish rule in South America.

events.title: Callao surrenders
events.description: The last Spanish garrison in South America gives up the fortress at Callao.

events.title: Peru-Bolivian Confederation
events.description: Santa Cruz unites the two republics. Chile and Argentina go to war to break it up within three years.

events.title: Ramon Castilla and the guano boom
events.description: Seabird droppings from the offshore islands become the world's best fertiliser and fund the state for a generation.

events.title: Chinese indentured labourers arrive
events.description: Around 100,000 workers are brought to the guano islands and coastal plantations under brutal contracts.

events.title: Slavery and indigenous tribute abolished
events.description: Castilla ends both, funded by guano revenue, though debt peonage persists in the highlands.

events.title: Battle of Callao
events.description: Peru and its allies repel a Spanish fleet attempting to reassert control over the guano islands.

events.title: First civilian president elected
events.description: Manuel Pardo takes office, breaking decades of military rule, and pushes railway construction.

events.title: War of the Pacific begins
events.description: Chile invades over the nitrate fields. Peru loses its navy, its southern provinces and its solvency.

events.title: Chilean occupation of Lima
events.description: Chilean troops hold the capital for over two years and remove the contents of the National Library.

events.title: Treaty of Ancon
events.description: Peru cedes Tarapaca. The defeat provokes a long reckoning about race, nation and the state.

events.title: Aristocratic Republic begins
events.description: Nicolas de Pierola takes power, opening thirty years of civilian oligarchic rule and export-led growth.

events.title: Hiram Bingham reaches Machu Picchu
events.description: The Yale explorer publicises the site to the world, and later ships thousands of artefacts to the United States.

events.title: Leguia's Oncenio begins
events.description: Augusto Leguia rules for eleven years on foreign loans and public works, ending in the Depression.

events.title: Leguia overthrown
events.description: The Depression collapses export revenue and the army removes Leguia, opening decades of instability.

events.title: Trujillo uprising
events.description: An APRA rising is crushed and hundreds are executed at Chan Chan, poisoning civil-military relations for decades.

events.title: War with Ecuador
events.description: Peru occupies disputed Amazonian territory, confirmed by the Rio Protocol the following year.

events.title: Odria seizes power
events.description: An eight-year military government represses APRA while riding a postwar export boom.

events.title: Mass migration to Lima accelerates
events.description: Highland families settle the desert margins; the capital grows from 600,000 to several million within a generation.

events.title: Velasco's military government
events.description: A left-wing junta nationalises oil and mining and launches sweeping agrarian reform, breaking the old landed estates.

events.title: Agrarian reform decreed
events.description: Nine million hectares are expropriated and Quechua is later made an official language.

events.title: Ancash earthquake
events.description: A quake and landslide bury Yungay and kill around 70,000 people, the deadliest disaster in Andean history.

events.title: Shining Path launches its war
events.description: The Maoist insurgency burns ballot boxes in Chuschi. Twenty years of conflict will kill nearly 70,000 people.

events.title: Garcia's first term and hyperinflation
events.description: Debt default and monetary expansion produce inflation above 7,000 per cent by 1990.

events.title: Fujimori elected
events.description: An unknown agronomist beats Mario Vargas Llosa and imposes drastic stabilisation known as the Fujishock.

events.title: Self-coup and capture of Guzman
events.description: Fujimori closes Congress; months later Shining Path's leader is arrested in Lima and the insurgency breaks.

events.title: Japanese embassy hostage crisis
events.description: MRTA guerrillas hold 72 hostages for four months before a commando assault ends the siege.

events.title: Fujimori flees to Japan
events.description: Corruption videos bring down the government; he resigns by fax and is later jailed for human rights crimes.

events.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission reports
events.description: It finds nearly 70,000 dead, three quarters of them Quechua-speaking, and indicts both Shining Path and the state.

events.title: Pisco earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 8.0 quake kills around 500 people and destroys much of the southern coastal city.

events.title: Mining boom and social conflict
events.description: A decade of high copper and gold prices lifts millions out of poverty while provoking sustained protest over water and land.

events.title: Pandemic and political crisis
events.description: Peru records the world's highest per-capita Covid death rate and cycles through three presidents in a week.

events.title: Castillo removed after self-coup attempt
events.description: The president tries to dissolve Congress, is impeached and arrested, and protests in the south are met with dozens of deaths.
